operations_plan.summary: Remove the existing flat-pin plug and establish reusable cable-end, insertion-axis, and symmetry references for the Europlug replacement.

steps.description: Isolate the existing mains plug section S08 and remove or suppress solid 19 in its entirety, including the molded body faces 404-413 and both apparent flat contacts represented by faces 394-403. Do not modify the power-lead solid 18 or its swept cable and enclosure-side strain-relief geometry. The replacement will occupy the removed plug's terminal region.

Capture the cable termination before rebuilding the plug. Use cord attachment end face 393 as the cable-end attachment plane and use adjacent terminal jacket faces 384-392 to determine the cable centerline, local width, thickness, and tangent direction. Preserve these faces and the upstream cord routing exactly. Define a local plug axis through the cable endpoint, initially aligned with the former plug and pin projection direction inferred from plug nose face 412 and the longitudinal edges of former pin faces 394-403.

Create a plug symmetry datum plane containing the local plug axis and cable centerline. Create a pin-layout datum plane normal to the plug axis at the former plug nose location, using face 412 as the positional reference. Place the pin-pattern origin at the midpoint between the two former contacts. Retain the current overall plug orientation relative to the cable unless this causes interference with the cord; manufacturer-specific Europlug styling and any alternative orientation remain unresolved because no reference product is specified.

operations_plan.summary: Create a compact, symmetric molded Europlug body and cable strain relief approximating the recognizable CEE 7/16 form.

steps.description: On the pin-layout datum plane from OP01_ST03, sketch the front profile of a generic CEE 7/16 Europlug body. Make the profile symmetric about both the pin-midpoint centerline and the principal body centerline. Use a flattened rounded-lozenge or compact oval contour rather than the former angular block. If the model uses millimetres at real scale, target approximately 32-35 mm overall width and 13-14 mm overall thickness; otherwise scale these proportions consistently while preserving the standard pin dimensions in OP03. Constrain the future pin centers symmetrically within this profile.

Create one or more offset cross-section planes toward the cable endpoint. Sketch progressively smaller, rounded profiles centered on the plug axis, ending in a compact neck surrounding the preserved cable termination at face 393. Loft from the broad pin-side profile to the smaller rear profile over an approximate body length of 28-32 mm when working at real millimetre scale. Maintain a smooth, symmetric taper typical of a molded Europlug and avoid abrupt shoulders or undercuts that would conflict with hand handling or molding.

Join the lofted plug body to a short molded cable-entry neck centered on face 393. Add a tapered strain-relief boot extending from the plug body onto only the minimal terminal portion of the cable. Form three to five shallow circumferential or transverse flex ribs with rounded roots, decreasing in size toward the cable. Match the boot's terminal section to the measured cable envelope from faces 385-392, and preserve the cable centerline, length, diameter, and upstream sweep.

Apply realistic molded-product edge treatment to the new plug body. Add continuous fillets around the front perimeter, tapered side transitions, rear shoulder, and strain-relief rib roots. Use fillet radii proportional to local wall size, with larger radii on hand-contacting outer edges and smaller radii at detail transitions. Keep the pin seating face locally planar and normal to the plug axis so both pins can be seated at an equal depth.

operations_plan.summary: Replace the former flat contacts with exactly two symmetric, parallel, circular Europlug pins and add realistic pin-root detailing.

steps.description: On the new planar plug nose, sketch exactly two equal circles. Place their centers symmetrically about the body centerline with a nominal center-to-center spacing of 19 mm for a real-scale CEE 7/16 Europlug. Constrain both circles to a nominal diameter of 4.0 mm. These standard-based dimensions implement a realistic generic Europlug because the request specifies no manufacturer-specific dimensions.

Extrude the two circular profiles outward from the plug nose as two cylindrical pins. Make both pin axes parallel to each other and parallel to the local plug insertion axis, with equal projection and equal seating depth. At real millimetre scale, use approximately 19 mm exposed pin length. Ensure there are exactly two pins and no remnant of the original flat-contact geometry.

Add small coaxial annular collars or molded recesses where the two pins enter the plug nose, keeping both roots identical and symmetric. For a contemporary realistic appearance, represent insulated pin-base sleeves over the rear portion of each pin while retaining exposed conductive cylindrical tips; keep the overall outside diameter nominally 4.0 mm and preserve equal total pin length. Model the sleeves as separate material regions or split faces rather than adding nonstandard radial bulk.

Apply small equal chamfers or rounded edges to both pin tips to remove sharp circular edges and mimic manufactured insertion tips. Add small fillets at the pin roots where permitted without changing the required pin diameter or spacing. Verify that corresponding left and right pin features are mirror-symmetric and terminate on a common plane.

operations_plan.summary: Validate the Europlug replacement, cable continuity, symmetry, clearances, and preservation of all non-plug appliance geometry.

steps.description: Check that the rebuilt S08 replacement consists of a compact molded Europlug body, cable-entry strain relief, and exactly two round cylindrical pins. Confirm nominal pin diameter of 4.0 mm, nominal center spacing of 19 mm, equal exposed length, parallel axes, symmetric placement, and a common insertion direction. Confirm that no planar blade geometry from faces 394-403 remains.

Run interference and continuity checks at the new plug-to-cord transition. Verify that the molded neck and strain relief meet the preserved cable terminal at face 393 without a gap, excessive overlap, sharp internal corner, or change to the upstream cable route. If a solid union is required by the modeling format, unite only the new insulating body or boot with the terminal cable jacket while keeping conductive pin regions separately identifiable.

Inspect the replacement in the existing +Z, -Z, +X, -X, +Y, -Y, and isometric views. Confirm that the new body follows the current cable endpoint and orientation, reads visually as a real Type C Europlug, and remains clear of the appliance enclosure, support feet, U-shaped cradle, and visible internal components throughout the represented configuration.

Perform a final preservation comparison against the original model. Confirm that solids 0-18 are unchanged except for the minimal terminal interface on solid 18 required to join the new strain relief. Preserve all enclosure dimensions, seams, openings, internal components, carafe geometry, support feet, external cradle and pivots, cord diameter, cord length, and cord routing. Assign execution-time solid identifiers to the new body, sleeves, and pins while retaining their semantic grouping as the replacement mains plug section S08.
